title: TE Carl W. Bogue, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension
disposition_detail: Specifications of continued noncompliance and constitutional violation were sustained; contumacy was not sustained; recommendations for remedial action were adopted.
first_summary: The complainants challenged Ascension Presbytery’s resolution refusing to comply with directions from the Eleventh General Assembly concerning an ordination examination. The case record reports that continued noncompliance and constitutional violation were sustained, but contumacy was not sustained, and remedial recommendations were adopted.
summary: Ascension Presbytery was challenged for resolving not to comply with prior General Assembly directions concerning an ordination examination. The case was sustained as to continued noncompliance and constitutional violation, but not as to contumacy; remedial recommendations were adopted. The supplied text contains the complaint rather than the operative judgment, so it does not disclose the adjudicative reasoning or the specific remedial measures.

sources.supports: Case identity, complaint posture, challenged refusal to comply, prior Assembly directions, requested redress, and reported disposition.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The heading identifies Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension and the CJB/12th Assembly; the complaint caption appears at lines 1–5 and 13–15 (printed p. 169).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint attacks Presbytery’s March 10, 1984 resolution refusing compliance with specified directions from the Eleventh General Assembly (lines 15, 19–25, 43–49; printed pp. 169–170).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The source header reports that noncompliance and constitutional-violation specifications were sustained, contumacy was not sustained, and remedial recommendations were adopted (line 3). No operative reasoning appears.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The contumacy allegation failed even though the other specifications succeeded; the specific remedy is omitted (line 3).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The complaint describes the Eleventh General Assembly’s earlier annulment and corrective directions in Judicial Case #2 (lines 19–25), but that incorporated decision is not supplied.
